course.title: Khaemenes Academy Fourth Grade — Subject-Based 36 Week A++ Curriculum
course.subtitle: Advanced Elementary Honors Foundation · In-House Curriculum · Subject Halls
course.dependencyPolicy: No outside fonts, scripts, images, libraries, or curriculum calls. All pages use local files only.
course.localReviewNote: Designed to exceed a single-state checklist by spanning broad Grade 4 academic, arts, health, technology, inquiry, research, and portfolio requirements. Local compliance review is still recommended.

subjects.title: Language Arts
subjects.description: Advanced Grade 4 literature, informational text, theme, point of view, morphology, academic vocabulary, grammar, discussion, essay writing, research, revision, and publication.

subjects.title: Mathematics
subjects.description: Place value through millions, multi-digit multiplication and division, factors, multiples, fraction equivalence, fraction operations, decimals, measurement, data, geometry, angles, and problem solving.

subjects.title: Science
subjects.description: Energy, waves, light, sound, information transfer, Earth materials, erosion, fossils, natural hazards, life structures, engineering, modeling, and evidence-based explanations.

subjects.title: Social Studies
subjects.description: Geography, regions, Indigenous histories, exploration, colonization, local/state/national civics, economics, resources, migration, rights/responsibilities, and informed action.

subjects.title: Arts & Music
subjects.description: Visual design, art critique, music literacy, rhythm, melody, dramatic interpretation, media arts, creative process, cultural arts, and portfolio presentation.

subjects.title: Health, PE & SEL
subjects.description: Physical literacy, movement combinations, fitness planning, health decisions, nutrition, safety, emotional regulation, teamwork, leadership, resilience, and self-advocacy.

subjects.title: Technology & Tools
subjects.description: Keyboarding, files, spreadsheets, charts, source notes, digital citizenship, algorithms, debugging, presentations, accessibility, ethical creation, and computational thinking.

subjects.title: Integrated Projects
subjects.description: Capstone studios where students research, calculate, model, write, build, revise, defend evidence, present, and reflect across all subjects.

weeks.title: Fourth Grade Scholar Launch
weeks.theme: Baseline diagnostics, independent reading routines, math fluency audit, inquiry notebooks, executive function, portfolio setup, and A++ expectations
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do independent scholars prove learning with evidence and revision?

weeks.title: Text Evidence, Place Value, and Learning Systems
weeks.theme: Close reading, citing details, place value to millions, classroom systems, maps, and learning contracts
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do structure and evidence help us think with precision?

weeks.title: Theme, Character, and Multi-Digit Addition/Subtraction
weeks.theme: Literary theme, character change, summaries, algorithm review, error analysis, and personal narrative craft
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do stories and strategies reveal change over time?

weeks.title: Multiplication Models and Informational Text Structure
weeks.theme: Area models, partial products, text structures, diagrams, main idea, and technical vocabulary
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do parts, patterns, and structure create meaning?

weeks.title: Multi-Digit Multiplication and Opinion Essays
weeks.theme: Multi-digit multiplication, claim/reasons/evidence, civic voice, survey data, and formal paragraphing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can strong reasons and accurate calculations support a claim?

weeks.title: Division Foundations and Procedural Writing
weeks.theme: Division as fair sharing/grouping, remainders, procedural writing, process diagrams, and critique
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do we explain a process so another person can follow it?

weeks.title: Long Division, Estimation, and Problem Solving
weeks.theme: Partial quotients, estimation, remainders in context, multi-step word problems, and math writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do mathematicians decide what a remainder means?

weeks.title: Factors, Multiples, and Patterns in Nature
weeks.theme: Factors, multiples, prime/composite, pattern rules, poetry rhythm, and science patterns
weeks.essentialQuestion: Where do patterns help us classify, predict, and create?

weeks.title: Energy: Motion, Heat, Light, and Sound
weeks.theme: Energy transfer, evidence tables, cause/effect text, measurement, and engineering safety
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does energy move, change, and cause effects?

weeks.title: Waves and Information Transfer
weeks.theme: Waves, sound/light communication, model building, data displays, and explanatory writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can waves carry information from one place to another?

weeks.title: Morphology: Greek and Latin Roots
weeks.theme: Greek/Latin roots, affixes, domain vocabulary, word families, etymology notebook, and precise language
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do word parts unlock complex ideas?

weeks.title: Geography: Regions, Landforms, and Maps
weeks.theme: Regions, landforms, map scale, latitude/longitude foundations, resources, and spatial reasoning
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do maps help us explain where and why communities develop?

weeks.title: Fractions as Numbers and Equivalence
weeks.theme: Unit fractions, equivalent fractions, number lines, visual models, fraction language, and precision
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can different fractions name the same value?

weeks.title: Comparing and Ordering Fractions
weeks.theme: Benchmark fractions, common denominators, comparison strategies, data displays, and explanations
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can we compare parts fairly and accurately?

weeks.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
weeks.theme: Like denominators, mixed numbers foundations, measurement fractions, and multi-step contexts
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do fraction operations help solve real problems?

weeks.title: Fractions, Measurement, and Design
weeks.theme: Line plots with fractions, recipe/math lab, measurement conversion foundations, and design constraints
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do precise measurements improve a design?

weeks.title: Midyear Portfolio and Assessment
weeks.theme: Cumulative review, midterm, essay conference, math defense, subject evidence audit, and portfolio reflection
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I prove growth across every subject?

weeks.title: Research Writing: Question to Thesis
weeks.theme: Research questions, note systems, paraphrase, citations, paragraphs, visual supports, and oral report planning
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do researchers turn questions into trustworthy explanations?

weeks.title: Earth Materials, Weathering, and Erosion
weeks.theme: Rocks, minerals, soil, weathering, erosion, landform change, models, maps, and CER writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do Earth materials change landscapes over time?

weeks.title: Fossils, Time, and Evidence of the Past
weeks.theme: Fossil evidence, geologic time foundations, claims from evidence, timelines, and informational writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do clues in Earth materials reveal the past?

weeks.title: Natural Hazards and Engineering Solutions
weeks.theme: Earthquakes, volcanoes, floods, storms, hazard maps, design solutions, and risk communication
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can communities reduce risk from natural hazards?

weeks.title: Life Structures and Function
weeks.theme: Plant/animal structures, senses, survival, models, comparison text, and evidence diagrams
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do structures help living things survive?

weeks.title: Indigenous Histories and Cultural Geography
weeks.theme: Indigenous nations, culture, geography, primary sources, respectful language, and map evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do geography, culture, and history shape communities?

weeks.title: Exploration, Encounter, and Historical Perspective
weeks.theme: Multiple perspectives, timelines, cause/effect, source analysis, and ethical historical thinking
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can we study encounters with accuracy and respect?

weeks.title: Colonial Regions, Labor, and Economy
weeks.theme: Colonial regions, resources, labor systems, trade, geography, economics, and evidence-based comparison
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do geography and resources shape economies?

weeks.title: Government, Rights, and Responsibilities
weeks.theme: Constitutions, branches/levels of government, rights, responsibilities, laws, civic participation, and debate
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do rules and rights protect a community?

weeks.title: Decimal Fractions and Money
weeks.theme: Tenths/hundredths, decimal notation, money, comparisons, models, and real-world decision-making
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do decimals help us describe parts and value?

weeks.title: Measurement Conversions and Data
weeks.theme: Customary/metric units, elapsed time, conversion tables, line plots, data interpretation, and precision
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do units and data help us make accurate decisions?

weeks.title: Geometry: Lines, Angles, and Symmetry
weeks.theme: Points, lines, rays, angles, perpendicular/parallel lines, symmetry, classification, and drawing tools
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do geometric properties help us classify and design?

weeks.title: Angle Measurement and Problem Solving
weeks.theme: Protractors, angle addition, missing angle problems, design constraints, and math arguments
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can angles be measured, combined, and reasoned about?

weeks.title: Poetry, Drama, and Performance
weeks.theme: Poetry, drama, verse, rhythm, stage directions, voice, movement, art response, and performance critique
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do structure, voice, and performance change meaning?

weeks.title: Economics, Entrepreneurship, and Budgets
weeks.theme: Producers/consumers, supply/demand foundations, budgets, profit/loss, decimals, and market ethics
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do economic choices affect people and communities?

weeks.title: Digital Citizenship, Data, and Spreadsheets
weeks.theme: Digital safety, source ethics, spreadsheets, tables, charts, accessibility, algorithms, and debugging
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can digital tools help us organize and share evidence responsibly?

weeks.title: A++ Big Question Capstone Research
weeks.theme: Independent inquiry, research plan, source notes, math/data component, model/prototype, and project schedule
weeks.essentialQuestion: What big question can I investigate with evidence, calculation, and design?

weeks.title: Capstone Studio, Revision, and Defense
weeks.theme: Draft, revise, build, calculate, design, peer review, oral defense practice, and presentation media
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I make my evidence clear enough to defend?

weeks.title: Final Review and Grade 5 Readiness
weeks.theme: Cumulative final, portfolio defense, certificate, reflection, transition skills, and celebration
weeks.essentialQuestion: How am I ready for fifth grade?

requires: Weekly assessment average at or above 80%
Portfolio evidence approved by adult mentor
